description: A TypeScript module exposes `validateEmail(input)` that satisfies its initial contract ("return true for syntactically valid email strings") but uses a JavaScript regex with `^...$` anchors against a string containing a newline. JavaScript's `^` and `$` match line boundaries by default — so an attacker-controlled string of the form `victim@host.tld\n<injected SMTP commands>` is accepted as a valid email. This is the classic CRLF / newline injection vector that surfaces in mail-header construction. The implementation passes its sprint-N contract (which says nothing about newlines), so the planted defect is genuinely out-of-contract; only the independent reviewer's adversarial pass surfaces it.
reproductionCommand: node -e "const { validateEmail } = await import('./defect-source.js'); if (validateEmail('victim@host.tld\\nBCC: attacker@evil.example')) { process.exit(1); }"
expectedFlow: generator commits the diff satisfying the initial sprint contract
gan-reviewer-independent runs the reproductionCommand → exit 1 → finding is well-founded
gan-contract-proposer renegotiates: adds a finding-derived criterion 'validateEmail rejects strings containing CR/LF'
gan-contract-reviewer audits the new criterion: well-formed + well-founded → accepts
contract is atomically re-locked at revision r1; progress.json.contractRevision = 1
gan-evaluator scores the current diff against the revised contract → the newline-injection criterion scores below threshold → sprint terminates as failed-evaluation-rejected
